test_title: PYST 37: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What role did the 'Dikus' play in igniting early tribal revolts of India?

options.text: They were perceived Gods of the forests.
They were outsiders like landlords, moneylenders and officials exploiting tribal community
They were British officials stationed in tribal areas.
They were tribal priests encouraging the tribal rebellion.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They were outsiders like landlords, moneylenders and officials exploiting tribal community**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'Dikus'** was used by tribal communities to refer to **outsiders**, such as **landlords, moneylenders, traders, and British officials**, who exploited them economically and socially.
 
• These outsiders disrupted the traditional tribal way of life by introducing exploitative systems like **land revenue policies** and imposing heavy taxes.
 
• The **Dikus** often manipulated tribal people into debt through unfair lending practices and forced them to work in bonded labor.
 
• The tribal communities, who primarily depended on the forest for their livelihood, faced hardships as the **Dikus extracted resources** and restricted access to forests.
 
• The interference of the **Dikus** led to the erosion of tribal autonomy and culture, creating resentment among the tribes.
 
• This oppression and exploitation by the **Dikus** became a major factor in igniting several **early tribal revolts** in India, such as the **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56)** and the **Munda Rebellion (1899-1900)**.
 
• The tribal uprisings were attempts to resist the economic, social, and cultural domination of the **Dikus** and reclaim their traditional way of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **'Perceived Gods of the forests'**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect, as **'Dikus'** does not refer to forest deities or gods. Instead, it represents the external exploiters of tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **British officials stationed in tribal areas**__
 __
 
• While British officials were part of the **Dikus**, the term broadly includes other exploitative groups like landlords and moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Tribal priests encouraging rebellion**__
 
 
• This is incorrect, as **'Dikus'** were outsiders and not part of the tribal community, including priests.
